title: Orthogonal circles and a fixed-dimensional separated-distance counterexample
summary: A finite set of points in Euclidean space is distance-separated if the lengths of any two different unordered edges differ by at least one. Counting distances shows that an n-point distance-separated set has diameter at least binom(n,2), approximately n^2/2, and Erdős asked whether the diameter must be at least (1-o(1))n^2. Ho showed that the answer is no if the dimension may grow with n. The first version of this paper gave counterexamples with diameter below 0.74n^2 in a single fixed dimension.
